children: Equity benchmarks extended upward journey and rallied more than 1 percent on November 20 despite negative market breadth. About 2,067 stocks were under pressure compared to 1,268 stocks that advanced on the NSE. The momentum may remain strong in the market despite intermittent consolidation and profit booking. Here are some short-term trading ideas to watch:
Vaishnavi Jagtap, Senior Research Analyst – Technical at Axis Direct

Federal Bank is in a strong uptrend across all time frames, forming a series of higher tops and bottoms. The daily price action has confirmed a "flag" formation (continuation pattern) breakout at the Rs 369 level, along with huge volumes indicating resumption of the prior uptrend.

The stock is well placed above its 20-, 50-, 100-, and 200-day simple moving averages (SMAs). These averages are also inching up with the price rise, which reconfirms the bullish trend. The daily, weekly and monthly Relative Strength Index (RSI) is in favourable territory, indicating rising strength across all time frames.

With the current weekly gains of over 5 percent, EIH confirmed a breakout from the past one-year "descending triangle" pattern at around the Rs 327 level, accompanied by huge volumes, indicating a trend reversal. The daily Bollinger Band buy signal indicates increased momentum.

The stock is well placed above its 20, 50, 100 and 200-day SMAs. This reconfirms the bullish trend. The daily and weekly RSI is in favourable territory, indicating rising strength across all time frames.
Bajaj Holdings and Investment | CMP: Rs 11,669

On the weekly chart, Bajaj Holdings and Investment has surpassed the multi-month horizontal resistance zone of the Rs 11,580 level on a closing basis, indicating a bullish trend reversal on the larger time frame. On the daily chart, it has also broken out past the four-month "down-sloping trendline" breakout at the Rs 11,440 level, indicating a positive bias.

The stock is well placed above its 20, 50, 100 and 200-day SMAs. This reconfirms the bullish trend. The daily and weekly RSI is in favourable territory, indicating rising strength across all time frames.
Jatin Gedia, Vice President and Derivatives & Technical Research Analyst at Teji Mandi
Power Grid Corporation of India | CMP: Rs 269

Power Grid was consolidating within a narrowing range for the past couple of weeks. Last week, it broke out of that triangle consolidation on the upside suggesting resumption of the next leg of the upmove.

On the weekly charts, the stock formed a Bullish Engulfing candlestick pattern, which bullish implications. Momentum indicator on multiple time frames i.e weekly and daily time frame has a positive crossover which is a buy signal.
Thus, considering the price pattern breakout along with a bullish momentum setup suggests that the stock is poised for a strong upmove over the next few trading sessions.

Coromandel was consolidating after a rally from Rs 1,779 to Rs 2,054. It pulled back to the support cluster of Rs 1,940–1,950, which coincides with the 40-hour exponential moving average and the hourly lower bollinger band where it found renewed buying interest. This led to an upside breakout from the six-day consolidation, signalling the start of the next leg of the upmove.

Momentum indicator pulled back to the equilibrium line and triggered a fresh positive crossover which is a buy signal. Thus, both price and momentum setup suggest start of a fresh leg of upmove towards the daily upper Bollinger band at Rs 2,077.

Indian Hotels has been in an uptrend. For the past ten trading sessions, the stock was consolidating within Rs 875 - 900. On Friday, the stock broke out of that consolidation on the upside, suggesting start of the next leg of the rally.

The momentum indicator RSI is sustaining above the 60 level, and a bullish crossover keeps the bullish momentum intact. The stock is trading at an all-time high and the next resistance, according to the Fibonacci extension method is projected at Rs 949.
